summary: In a major regulatory milestone, the Federal Communications Commission has authorized SpaceX to deploy up to one million satellites for space-based data centers, though scientists remain skeptical over potential orbital debris risks. In human spaceflight, China launched the Shenzhou 24 mission to the Tiangong space station, sending three crew members into orbit, including Pakistan's first astronaut to visit the outpost. In planetary exploration, Europe’s Hera spacecraft captured its first close-up images of the crater created on asteroid Dimorphos by NASA’s DART mission, while Japan unveiled a prototype rover designed for lunar water prospecting. Scientific research reached new limits as astronomers discovered the most distant supermassive black hole-powered quasar on record, formed just 630 million years after the Big Bang, while NASA's Hubble Space Telescope conducted extensive star surveys to prepare for the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. Across defense space and aviation, SpaceX launched classified spy satellites for the U.S. Space Force, the U.S. Army fully fielded its first Dark Eagle hypersonic battery, and the Air Force awarded Boeing a $2.8 billion contract for additional KC-46 tankers alongside a $48.7 million contract for weather data from high-altitude balloons. In commercial industry transactions, Cerberus agreed to acquire Airbus U.S. Space & Defense, and BlackSky acquired data science firm EpochGeo. Looking ahead, observers should watch as NASA’s Europa Clipper completes its Earth flyby to gain the momentum required for its long journey to Jupiter's icy moon.
